reason: Conversation 1 followed the sensible path: it asked what the display showed and whether a door was blocked, got the customer to reveal the drawer left ajar, explained that this was the cause, had them silence the alarm with the bell button and monitor for -18 - a correct, honest, no-fault diagnosis reached in four tight turns. Conversation 2 opened with a shotgun wall of text including an unnecessary unplug reset, mixed Fahrenheit/Celsius, and raised 'faulty door switch, temperature sensor, or control board' before knowing anything, and it never actually established the root cause (it only listed 'was a drawer not pushed in?' as a question the customer never answered). Conversation 2 did better on food-safety guidance and model-number location, and Conversation 1 omitted a food check and attached an irrelevant 'sealed system' image, which keeps the margin slight rather than clear.
